summary_oneline: JiraToolkit gains Jinja2 template composition for issue descriptions and comment bodies, reusing the core TemplateEngine with a Jira-safe config (no autoescape) and a templates_dir / JIRA_TEMPLATES_DIR config knob.

constraints.statement: Description and comment body are passed to pycontribs JIRA unchanged; there is no markdown→wiki-markup/ADF conversion stage in the toolkit path
constraints.implication: rendered template output IS the final Jira wiki-markup/plain text; rendering must not HTML-escape and nothing downstream reformats it

constraints.statement: TemplateEngine defaults to select_autoescape keyed on file extension (.j2/.jinja/.html…) and StrictUndefined; its __init__ raises ValueError if a template dir does not exist
constraints.implication: the Jira engine must be built with JinjaConfig(autoescape=False), choose an explicit undefined policy, and be constructed lazily / tolerate a missing dir so toolkit construction never fails

constraints.statement: jinja2>=3.1 is already a hard dependency of ai-parrot and ai-parrot-tools
constraints.implication: no new dependency; no optional-extra gating needed

constraints.statement: ai-parrot-tools house style is a `templates_dir: Optional[Path]` constructor kwarg (msword/powerpoint/pdfprint); core style is TemplateEngine with template_dirs + in-memory templates (infographic_toolkit)
constraints.implication: expose `templates_dir` (+ optional in-memory `templates` mapping) on JiraToolkit and delegate to TemplateEngine internally

constraints.statement: Constructor settings resolve through _cfg() (navconfig → env), with JIRA_DEFAULT_* defaults and a per-project JIRA_WORKFLOW_PATH_<PROJECT> override map keyed by upper-cased project
constraints.implication: a JIRA_TEMPLATES_DIR env/navconfig key fits the precedent; per-project/per-issuetype template selection can mirror the workflow_paths lookup pattern

constraints.statement: test_init_signature_unchanged pins the exact __init__ parameter tuple
constraints.implication: adding templates_dir is an intentional baseline change and must update INIT_PARAMS_BASELINE in the same task

constraints.statement: All 10 external call sites of jira_create_issue / jira_add_comment use keyword arguments and never pass template-related params
constraints.implication: new OPTIONAL params (template, template_params) are backward compatible; existing callers keep today's verbatim behaviour

constraints.statement: ResearchNode enforces a 30 000-char description cap against Atlassian's 32 767 limit with summarize-then-truncate degradation
constraints.implication: a template can easily exceed the cap when given log excerpts; the toolkit renderer should at least guard/truncate or surface the length

constraints.statement: JiraToolkitConfig (Agent Studio) is extra=forbid and lists only auth/project fields
constraints.implication: if operators must set templates from Agent Studio, the model needs a templates_dir field; otherwise env/kwarg only

whats_new: A template rendering seam inside JiraToolkit: a lazily built parrot.template.TemplateEngine (JinjaConfig(autoescape=False)) loaded from `templates_dir` / JIRA_TEMPLATES_DIR plus optional in-memory `templates` mapping

Optional `template` (name) and `template_params` (dict) parameters on jira_create_issue / jira_add_comment (and optionally jira_update_issue); when `template` is set, the body is rendered with a context = call fields (project, summary, issuetype, labels, description, issue…) ∪ template_params, and the rendered string replaces description/body
A `jira_list_templates` read tool so an agent can discover available template names (LLM-facing)
Unit tests for rendering, strict/lenient undefined policy, autoescape-off, missing template error, and backward-compat (no template → unchanged behaviour)

extend the baseline tuple with the new kwarg(s)

Changing JiraInterface (read-only) or the pycontribs client

unknowns.question: Where do templates live and how are they configured — filesystem directory only (templates_dir kwarg + JIRA_TEMPLATES_DIR), also in-memory `templates` mapping for programmatic use, and/or exposed in Agent Studio (JiraToolkitConfig)?
plausible_answers: filesystem dir via kwarg/env only (simplest, mirrors msword/powerpoint)
both of the above + templates_dir in JiraToolkitConfig for Agent Studio
unknowns.user_answer: Dir + in-memory mapping — `templates_dir` kwarg / JIRA_TEMPLATES_DIR env for files, plus an optional `templates={name: source}` mapping for programmatic use (mirrors infographic_toolkit). Agent Studio exposure not required.

unknowns.question: How is a template selected — only explicitly by name per call (`template='bug'`), automatically by convention (`<PROJECT>/<issuetype>.j2` with a `_default`, like workflow_paths), or both (explicit wins, convention as fallback)?
plausible_answers: both: explicit name wins, else per-project/issuetype convention, else no template
unknowns.user_answer: Explicit wins, convention fallback — `template='bug'` when given; otherwise look up `<PROJECT>/<issuetype>` then `_default` (like workflow_paths); otherwise no template.

unknowns.question: What should happen when a template references a placeholder the caller did not provide — fail the tool call with the missing names (StrictUndefined), or render leniently (blank / leave `{{ name }}` visible)?
plausible_answers: strict: fail with a clear error listing missing variables (engine default)
lenient-visible: leave the placeholder text so the reviewer sees the gap
unknowns.user_answer: Strict — fail with names: the tool call fails with a clear error listing the missing variables (StrictUndefined).

unknowns.question: Should the LLM agent be able to discover and pick templates (a `jira_list_templates` tool + `template` as a tool parameter), or is templating operator-only configuration applied automatically?
plausible_answers: LLM-facing: list tool + template param (agent decides)
operator-only: auto-applied, no new tool params
both: auto-applied default, agent may override by name
unknowns.user_answer: Both — operator config auto-applies a default; the agent may list templates (`jira_list_templates`) and override by name via a `template` tool parameter.

unknowns.question: Scope: besides create (description) and add_comment (body), should jira_update_issue's description also accept a template?
unknowns.user_answer: Create + comment + update — same `template` / `template_params` seam on all three write paths.
